note: decodePacket: one Engine.IO v4 wire string back to a packet. Replies are {packet:{type:<name>,data:<string>,binary:<lowercase hex|null>}}. Upstream reports a parse failure in band, by returning its ERROR_PACKET ({type:"error",data:"parser error"}) instead of throwing; the node runner turns that into ok:false, which is the honest counterpart of the Go codec returning an error. `eio.decodeBinaryFrame` is the websocket path where the frame's raw bytes (given here as hex) are the packet.

cases.note: no data: upstream leaves data undefined, the port leaves it the empty string; both normalise to ""
the framing layer does not validate the handshake body
CLOSE has no payload in the protocol, but neither implementation rejects one
a MESSAGE carrying a Socket.IO EVENT
decodePacket has no notion of the record separator: it stays part of the data
"b" only means base64 when it is the FIRST character; here it is message data
"b"+base64 decodes to the bytes 00 ff 10 (hex) as a binary MESSAGE
explicit "=" padding, one payload byte
"b" alone is a zero-length binary MESSAGE, not an error

cases.deviation: Node's Buffer.from(s,"base64") silently ignores characters outside the base64 alphabet, so upstream accepts the frame and yields an empty payload; the port rejects it. Rejecting attacker-supplied garbage is the safer behaviour and is kept deliberately (API-DEVIATIONS.md, divergence W12).
Same lenient-base64 divergence as dec-binary-bad-base64: a single base64 character cannot encode any byte, upstream yields an empty payload, the port errors.

cases.deviation: Node's base64 decoder also accepts the base64url alphabet ("-" and "_"), so upstream decodes "b-_8" to bytes; base64.StdEncoding rejects them. Same lenient-base64 family as dec-binary-bad-base64 — the port stays strict about which alphabet a frame may use.
Node's base64 decoder skips embedded whitespace, so upstream accepts "bYW Jj" as "abc"; base64.StdEncoding rejects the space. Same lenient-base64 family as dec-binary-bad-base64.
